answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history, with schedulers as choosy as sable trappers taking only proven pelts. Rights scale with completed priced micro-tasks, assigned like a ripple spreading from each account's genesis, so new identities start weak and gain influence only through honest work. Mass-registering thousands of agents yields worthless shells: fees climb along the ridge of task difficulty, so faking identity costs more than any payout captured.
